THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY, B.M.SHYAM PRASAD J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is by the claimant in MVC No.336/2021 on the file of Senior Civil Judge and MACT,
Chittapur (for short 'the Tribunal').
The appellant seeks enhancement in the compensation of Rs.29,41,800/- as awarded by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has awarded the aforesaid amount under the following heads:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1101-DB 1. Loss of earning Rs.15,55,200/-
2. Pain and suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
3. Loss of income during laid Rs.36,000/-
up period 4. Cost of Transportation Rs.15,000/-
during hospitalization 5.

2 6.
Attendant charges incurred during Rs.9,600/- hospitalization 7.

Medical expenses Rs.5,06,000/-
8. Loss of amenities Rs.1,00,000/-
9. Cost of artificial limb and Rs.6,05,000/-
other medical assistances Total Rs.29,41,800/-
2.
There is no dispute that the appellant, who was aged 21 years at the time of the accident, was employed in a quarry with a certain specialized skill set.

On the date of the accident, he was traveling on his motorcycle and had stopped for a cup of tea along a roadside Dhaba when a Tanker, insured with the second respondent, coming from the opposite side hit him.
The appellant, as a consequence NC: 2023:KHC-K:1101-DB of this accident, has suffered injuries that has resulted in amputation of his right leg above knee.
3. The doctor, who is examined on behalf of the appellant, has deposed that the appellant has a permanent disablement of 90%.
The Tribunal, in the light of the undisputed circumstances and the evidence on record, has opined that the appellant's disability must be taken as 60% and income in a sum of Rs.12,000/- per month.
The appellant is aggrieved by the Tribunal's findings on these scores and also for lack of award under the heads of future attendant charges and loss of marriage prospects.

Sri. Sanjeev Kumar and Sri. Sanjay M.Joshi, the learned counsels for the contesting parties, are heard in the light of the aforesaid grievance, and the only question for consideration is whether there must be enhancement in the compensation as awarded by the Tribunal.
4. Sri. Sanjeev Kumar submits that the appellant, at a young age of 21 years, has suffered amputation of right leg above knee.

The appellant had good prospects because NC:
2023:KHC-K:1101-DB he was working at a stone quarry with specialized skills which is a back breaking job but also with significant potential for increased earning.
The appellant's earning abilities are seriously impaired and as such, the functional permanent disability must be taken as 100%.
Sri. Sanjeev Kumar reiterates the appellant's grievance about the lack of award under the heads of future attendant charges and loss of marriage prospects.

5. As against these submissions, Sri. Sanjay M.Joshi submits that the recent decision, including the decision in Gurpreet Kaur and others V/s United India Insurance Company Ltd. and others1, is to take the notified minimum wages with reasonable addition when there is no proof of actual income.

sentences.text: He argues that the notified minimum wage for the relevant period and the appropriate zone, given circumstances of the case, would be in a sum of Rs.13,406/-.

As regards the disablement, Sri. Sanjay M.Joshi submits that the schedule percentage of permanent disability is 60% where there is amputation 1 2022 SCC Online SC 1778 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1101-DB above knee under the Schedule appended to the Employees Compensation Act and this serves as a just yardstick to assess disablement.
The Tribunal, therefore, is justified in taking the disability at 60%.
On the ground of lack of award under the heads of future attendant charges and loss of marriage prospects, Sri.

sentences.text: Sanjay M.Joshi argues that that there cannot be any exaggerated award.

6. The requirement of law under the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act is to award just and reasonable of compensation which is uniform and consistent as the settled parameters subject to moderation depending on the peculiarities of each case.

It is undisputed that the appellant, who was aged 21 years at the time of accident, has suffered amputation of right leg above knee and at the time of accident was working as a skilled labour in a quarry.

These admitted facts show that the appellant's prospects in terms of future earning capacity is rather truncated, and the permanent disability, which has to be assessed on the scale of functional disability given the individual skills of the appellant is also impaired.
The disability and consequential NC: 2023:KHC-K:1101-DB loss of income must be examined in the backdrop of these circumstances without taking a pedantic approach.

7. This Court is of the considered view that circumstances justify taking the income of the appellant at Rs.14,250/-, a sum as per the norms evolved for settlement in Lok-Adalath when there is no proof of actual income and the accident is of the year 2022.
The permanent disability must also be assessed pragmatically with an unavoidable element of estimation.
The appellant, who could avail the use of artificial leg, can adopt to another vocation.

Hence, it would not be a case for 100%
disability.
This Court must take permanent disability at 75% as against 60% taken by the Tribunal.
The appellant would also be entitled to addition of 40% towards future prospects.

8. The appellant, if the loss of future income is computed taking the permanent disability at 75% and the monthly income at Rs.14,250/- with the necessary addition towards loss of future prospects retaining the other parameters adopted by the Tribunal, would be entitled for a NC:
2023:KHC-K:1101-DB sum of Rs.32,31,900 /- towards loss of future earning as against a sum of Rs.15,55,200/-.

The computation will be as follows:

The appellant must also be granted just and reasonable amount towards loss of marriage prospects and costs to be incurred to avail the assistance of attendants in future.

4 Rs.3,00,000/- is found just and proper under these heads.
